item.title: Europe's borders, the end of 1947 (data for lessons) v0.3
item.snippet: Country borders in Europe on 31 December 1947, after the peace treaties of 1947 took effect. Draft for review: private until the source's licence is confirmed.
item.description:
Country borders in Europe on 31 December 1947, after the peace treaties of 1947 took effect: 30 areas, each with its name at the time, its status (independent, colony, mandate or occupied), who controlled it if it was not independent, and the dates between which this border was in force.

One of four layers (July 1914, 1925, January 1938, end of 1947) for comparing Europe before and after each world war's settlement.

Limits: the source leaves out the smallest states (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, Liechtenstein) and some special territories (the Saar; in 1947 the Free Territory of Trieste and Berlin's sectors), and draws the Soviet Union as one area. Coastlines are simplified. The layer is clipped at 60 degrees east.

Source: CShapes 2.0: Schvitz, Girardin, Ruegger, Weidmann, Cederman and Gleditsch (2022), Mapping the International System, 1886-2019, Journal of Conflict Resolution 66(1); ETH Zurich.

Data version 0.3 (19 November 2026), draft.
